validated: 2026-10-21 against real samples (full static extraction: strings, imports, resources, signature, section hashes)
collector: static analysis + live download interception (winhttp proxy)

module_dll.note: payload downloaded from /launcherDownload on 2026-10-21. hash changes per build: high-confidence hit, NOT the only rule.

code_signature.subject: CN=Prestige Software Development, O=Prestige Software Development, S=Limburg, C=NL
code_signature.issuer: CN=Sectigo Public Code Signing CA R36, O=Sectigo Limited, C=GB
code_signature.timestamp_authority: CN=Sectigo Public Time Stamping Signer R37, O=Sectigo Limited, C=GB
code_signature.note: VERY useful IOC: the serial/thumbprint survive a rebuild because the seller reuses the cert until it expires. Treat a valid signature from this subject as malicious, not benign.

launcher.note: Rich header + section MD5s are stable per-build and survive file renaming/rewrapping.

module.packer: VMProtect (.vm_sec + .vlizer), both sections present = strong indicator

version_resource.LegalCopyright: Copyright (C) 2026 Prestige Software Development. All rights reserved.
version_resource.note: OriginalFilename / InternalName survive a file rename and are read by most EDRs.

manifest.note: the assemblyIdentity string is embedded in the RT_MANIFEST resource - independent of the string table.

network.storage: UTF-16 in the binary (WinHTTP config is wchar_t) - ASCII-only scans miss this
network.note: the POST with no user-agent from WinHTTP is distinctive; curl/requests are blocked by Cloudflare.

validation.true_positive: both real samples fire their respective rules

limitations: hashes and host change on every rebuild/rebrand. cert serial/thumbprint, PDB paths and VMProtect sections are the most stable anchors. self-destruct is temporal and cannot be caught by a single static scan. see behavioral.md for runtime indicators.
